before.supportingExcerpt: Groove geometry helps explain common peptide lengths without imposing a hard upper limit. Wieczorek and colleagues' 2017 review describes the class-I groove as closed at both ends, usually holding 8 to 10 residues, and the open class-II groove as usually holding 13 to 25. It also describes longer class-I ligands, including solved HLA-A2 complexes with 15-residue peptides. A reported range around 11 is therefore not a ceiling for every class-I ligand. CD4 help does not demonstrate the same target's class-I display. Some CD4 cells can themselves be cytotoxic: Cachot and colleagues directly tested tumour-specific human CD4 cells against tumour cells in defined assays. That result does not make every CD4 response cytotoxic or establish a treatment benefit.
before.explanation: Class I and II identities, usual cellular routes and CD8/CD4 partners, typical peptide lengths, two inherited copies/up-to-six classical variants, allele-specific grooves and display are carried as common routes rather than absolute rules. Named current field passage inspected for its assigned teaching; primary evidence keeps the earlier recorded depth unless separately listed as a fresh read. This does not re-certify all older assertions in the owner.
